title: AI Tech Packs Beats Excel & Illustrator - Build Specs Fast
summary: Should you keep Excel and Illustrator or switch to AI Tech Packs? Compare drawing, measurements, editing, pricing and the files you send to your factory.
body_markdown:
You can keep Illustrator for drawing and refining your artwork. AI Tech Packs helps with the tech pack around it: draft flats, measurements, materials, editing, and downloads. You can also open the editable SVG flat sketches in Illustrator and check how they fit your work.


Yes, if those are the formats your factory accepts. Tech Pack membership includes PDF and Excel downloads and Factory Share links. Buying one tech pack includes downloads for that pack. Flat Sketch membership alone does not include tech pack downloads. Ask your factory about any templates or file requirements before sending it.


It depends on the garment, the image you upload, and the details you give it. Try a style you know and compare the draft with your approved pack. Check the measurements, grading, fabrics, construction, artwork, tolerances, and fit. That will give you a better idea of the work involved for your own styles.


Yes. You can change measurements, grading, materials, colorways, artwork, placements, and construction notes before saving and downloading the pack. Your technical designer still checks and approves the details.


Yes. You can edit size charts and grading in the pack. Use your own base measurements, grade rules, and tolerances, then check the fit through patterns and samples. Treat generated values as a starting point.


Yes. With Tech Pack membership, you can queue up to 10 styles in a batch and organize the packs into collections with production statuses. Check each pack before sending it to your factory.


Keep them if your spreadsheets, formulas, artwork, and factory templates work well for you. Try AI Tech Packs if setting up packs and copying between files takes too much time. You can use it alongside the tools you already have.
